title: The Devil to the Moon: tarot card meanings
description: Tarot card meanings for The Devil, The Tower, The Star and The Moon (XV to XVIII), upright and reversed, with tips for reading these cards in a spread.

scenes.headline: The Devil to the Moon: tarot card meanings
scenes.caption: Major arcana XV to XVIII cover attachment, upheaval, hope and uncertainty. Here is what each tarot card traditionally means, upright and reversed.
scenes.vo: Major arcana XV to XVIII cover attachment, upheaval, hope and uncertainty. Here is what each tarot card traditionally means, upright and reversed.

scenes.headline: The Devil
scenes.caption: Two small figures are chained loosely to a horned figure on a pedestal. Attachment, constraint, temptation, the shadow side.
scenes.vo: The Devil. Two small figures are chained loosely to a horned figure on a pedestal. Attachment, constraint, temptation, the shadow side.

scenes.headline: The Tower
scenes.caption: Lightning strikes a tall tower, and figures fall from it. Upheaval, sudden change, revelation, structures giving way.
scenes.vo: The Tower. Lightning strikes a tall tower, and figures fall from it. Upheaval, sudden change, revelation, structures giving way.

scenes.headline: The Star
scenes.caption: A figure kneels at a pool, pouring water onto the land and into the pool, under a large star surrounded by smaller ones.
scenes.vo: The Star. A figure kneels at a pool, pouring water onto the land and into the pool, under a large star surrounded by smaller ones.
